root_cause.text: The vt alternate-screen save/restore logic kept a saved `vc_saved_uni_lines` buffer allocated for old `vc_rows`/`vc_cols` dimensions and restored it after a resize, because `vc_do_resize()` did not reallocate it once `enter_alt_screen()` had set `vc_uni_lines` to `NULL`, leading to out-of-bounds access in unicode screen operations.
root_cause.evidence: The commit states that after `enter_alt_screen()` saves `vc_uni_lines` into `vc_saved_uni_lines` and nulls `vc_uni_lines`, a later resize "skips reallocating the unicode buffer because `vc_uni_lines` is NULL," while `vc_saved_uni_lines` still points to the old allocation; the patch then adds a dimension mismatch check in `leave_alt_screen()` and frees the saved buffer instead of restoring it when `vc_saved_rows/cols != vc_rows/cols` because "restoring it would cause out-of-bounds accesses."

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a local uni_lines_stale flag in leave_alt_screen() to support upcoming stale unicode-line handling logic.
intent_record.what: A new local boolean variable named uni_lines_stale was added to the function leave_alt_screen(struct vc_data *vc) alongside the existing local declarations.
intent_record.how: As shown in this hunk alone, runtime behavior does not change yet because the added variable is only declared and not used within the displayed code; it prepares the function for subsequent logic that will track whether unicode line state is stale.

intent_record.intent_summary: Avoid out-of-bounds access when leaving the alternate screen after a resize by discarding stale saved unicode screen data instead of restoring it.
intent_record.what: The unconditional call to vc_uniscr_set(vc, vc->vc_saved_uni_lines) was replaced with logic that checks whether the saved screen dimensions differ from the current console dimensions using vc->vc_saved_rows != vc->vc_rows || vc->vc_saved_cols != vc->vc_cols. A comment explaining the resize case was added, a uni_lines_stale condition was introduced, and when stale the code now calls vc_uniscr_free(vc->vc_saved_uni_lines); otherwise it restores the saved unicode screen with vc_uniscr_set(vc, vc->vc_saved_uni_lines).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents restoring a saved unicode screen buffer that was allocated for old console dimensions after the console was resized while in the alternate screen. Instead of risking out-of-bounds access by reusing mismatched saved data, the code frees the stale buffer and allows the unicode screen state to be rebuilt later, while still preserving the old behavior when dimensions match.

The change directly targets the root cause: stale saved unicode screen buffers from the alternate screen being restored after a resize. Discarding outdated saved unicode data on exit from alt-screen prevents the out-of-bounds access caused by mismatched vc_saved_uni_lines dimensions.

candidates.rationale: This restores the previously saved unicode-line buffer unconditionally when leaving the alternate screen. If the console was resized while in alt-screen mode, vc_saved_uni_lines may still be sized for the old dimensions, so reattaching it causes later unicode screen operations to access stale, undersized storage out of bounds.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement unconditionally restores the previously saved unicode screen buffer when leaving alternate-screen mode. If a resize occurred while in alt-screen mode, vc_saved_uni_lines may still reflect the old vc_rows/vc_cols allocation, so reattaching it makes subsequent unicode screen operations use stale undersized storage, causing out-of-bounds access.
